headline: University of Oldenburg physicists used two crossing laser pulses to create fully three-dimensional light and drive electrons into quantum states previously only predicted in theory.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed lab physics with long-term rather than near-term use; reported by a science-news site.
importance_line: It gives physicists a new tool to study and control how light affects electrons and chiral molecules, but it is basic research with no product yet.
summary: Bioengineer.org, relaying a Scienmag report, says physicists at Germany's University of Oldenburg crossed two ultrashort laser pulses of different colours to make light whose electric field oscillates in all three directions. Tested on potassium atoms, the method excited electrons into quantum states that had only been described in theory and made them visible, in a paper in Physical Review Research.
notes: Article credits Scienmag (Katie Riggs, 4 Oct 2026); source follows that chain.
